records.originalText: Tom is the most handsome actor in the world.
records.finalText: Tom is the most handsome actor in the world.
records.rationale: The world-wide actor superlative is an unbounded ranking with no speaker or comparison basis.

records.originalText: Tom attributed his failure in the exam to illness.
records.finalText: Tom attributed his failure in the exam to illness.
records.rationale: Attributed his failure to illness is a natural reporting collocation for one exam outcome.

records.originalText: Tom's report leaves much to be desired.
records.finalText: Tom's report leaves much to be desired.
records.rationale: Leaves much to be desired is a conventional idiom evaluating a particular report.

records.originalText: All but Tom were present.
records.finalText: All but Tom were present.
records.rationale: Pragmatic repeat of the published all-but-one-were-present example; Tom merely identifies the missing attendee.

records.originalText: Tom's hobby is collecting photos of cars.
records.finalText: Tom's hobby is collecting photos of cars.
records.rationale: The collecting-photos gerund phrase naturally names a specific person's hobby.

records.originalText: A good student like Tom brings honor to our class.
records.finalText: A good student like Tom brings honor to our class.
records.rationale: Brings honor to our class is a grammatical situated evaluation, without a group-wide generalization.

records.originalText: I got Tom to mend my shoes.
records.finalText: I got Tom to mend my shoes.
records.rationale: Got Tom to mend uses a correct object-plus-infinitive causative with a concrete repair task.

records.originalText: It is Tom's ambition to go to the moon.
records.finalText: It is Tom's ambition to go to the moon.
records.rationale: The anticipatory-it construction and moon-travel ambition are coherent and clearly personal.

records.originalText: Please give my best regards to Tom.
records.finalText: Please give my best regards to Tom.
records.rationale: Repeats the published give-my-regards-to-Tom message, adding only please and best.

records.originalText: There is little, if any, hope that Tom will win the election.
records.finalText: There is little, if any, hope that Tom will win the election.
records.rationale: Little if any appropriately qualifies hope within a complete election prediction.

records.originalText: When Tom lost his wallet, he was out of luck.
records.finalText: When Tom lost his wallet, he was out of luck.
records.rationale: The wallet-loss frame anchors the idiomatic out of luck expression in a specific event.

records.originalText: Tom owes what he is today to his wife.
records.finalText: Tom owes what he is today to his wife.
records.rationale: Owes what he is today to is a valid embedded-clause expression of personal gratitude.

records.originalText: Tom is at the door. Please ask him in.
records.finalText: Tom is at the door. Please ask him in.
records.rationale: The door location and ask-him-in request form a complete and coherent short utterance.

records.originalText: Tom ran and ran, until at last he saw the telephone booth.
records.finalText: Tom ran and ran, until at last he saw the telephone booth.
records.rationale: Repeated ran emphasizes continued effort; the until clause supplies the endpoint naturally.

records.originalText: Give me your passport, Tom. I'll keep it in my safe.
records.finalText: Give me your passport, Tom. I'll keep it in my safe.
records.rationale: The direct passport request and promise of storage form a coherent personal safekeeping offer.

records.originalText: Tommy couldn't answer the last question.
records.finalText: Tommy couldn't answer the last question.
records.rationale: Could not answer and the final question identify a clear past inability.

records.originalText: The tomato is a vegetable, not a fruit.
records.finalText: The tomato is a vegetable, not a fruit.
records.rationale: The vegetable-not-fruit assertion confuses culinary and botanical categories without specifying either.

records.originalText: What train goes to the center of town?
records.finalText: What train goes to the center of town?
records.rationale: The transport question identifies the destination and is natural as a route enquiry.

records.originalText: What subway goes to the center of town?
records.finalText: What subway goes to the center of town?
records.rationale: Repeats 37470's town-center transport enquiry with subway substituted for train.

records.originalText: Ask whichever of the boys you see first.
records.finalText: Ask whichever of the boys you see first.
records.rationale: Whichever of the boys you see first provides a clear selection condition in a complete request.

records.originalText: Sales have dropped off at every big department store.
records.finalText: Sales have dropped off at every big department store.
records.rationale: Every big department store is an unbounded sales assertion without a market or time scope.

records.originalText: It matters very little what college you graduated from.
records.finalText: It matters very little what college you graduated from.
records.rationale: The importance of college origin is a sweeping value judgment without a stated decision context.

records.originalText: I'm thinking about which college might be best for me.
records.finalText: I'm thinking about which college might be best for me.
records.rationale: The deliberative statement uses an embedded which clause naturally and remains personal.

records.originalText: A full description of him has been circulated in every newspaper.
records.finalText: A full description of him has been circulated in every newspaper.
records.rationale: The present-perfect passive describes circulation of one description; every newspaper is contextual narrative scope.

records.originalText: Every girl cannot be a ballerina.
records.finalText: Every girl cannot be a ballerina.
records.rationale: Every girl cannot is scope-ambiguous between none and not all; fixing it would require choosing the source meaning.

records.originalText: There is an exception to every rule.
records.finalText: There is an exception to every rule.
records.rationale: The exception-to-every-rule maxim is an unframed universal and logical overgeneralization.

records.originalText: How do you want them?
records.finalText: How do you want them?
records.rationale: Them lacks any item or preparation anchor, leaving an entirely context-dependent question.

records.originalText: How do you think I learned to speak English?
records.finalText: How do you think I learned to speak English?
records.rationale: The how-do-you-think question correctly embeds a statement-order clause about language learning.

records.originalText: How did you come by an admission ticket for the auto show free of charge?
records.finalText: How did you come by an admission ticket for the auto show free of charge?
records.rationale: Come by and free of charge are natural expressions in a complete ticket-acquisition question.

records.originalText: How can you tell an Englishman from an American?
records.finalText: How can you tell an Englishman from an American?
records.rationale: The nationality-identification question presupposes reliable group markers without any linguistic or contextual framing.

records.originalText: What sports do you go in for?
records.finalText: What sports do you go in for?
records.rationale: Go in for is a valid British expression for participating in sports.

records.originalText: Which platform is it on?
records.finalText: Which platform is it on?
records.rationale: The platform question leaves it without a named train or service, weakening independent usefulness.

records.originalText: Which concert did you choose to attend?
records.finalText: Which concert did you choose to attend?
records.rationale: Choose to attend is a natural verb-infinitive pattern in a complete concert question.

records.originalText: What gate do I board at?
records.finalText: What gate do I board at?
records.rationale: Board at a gate is natural airport usage and the question supplies the required location type.

records.originalText: How long have you been ill?
records.finalText: How long have you been ill?
records.rationale: The present-perfect duration question about one person's illness is grammatical and offers no clinical advice.

records.originalText: How soon can I get to Tokyo?
records.finalText: How soon can I get to Tokyo?
records.rationale: How soon correctly asks the earliest arrival time at a named destination.

records.originalText: How long will it take to get well?
records.finalText: How long will it take to get well?
records.rationale: The recovery-time question makes no unverified prediction and is complete direct speech.

records.originalText: How soon will this laundry be ready?
records.finalText: How soon will this laundry be ready?
records.rationale: The how-soon question about laundry readiness is natural service-counter speech.

records.originalText: Anyway, I gave it my best shot.
records.finalText: Anyway, I gave it my best shot.
records.rationale: Gave it my best shot is a complete idiomatic report of effort, though the activity remains implicit.

records.originalText: In any case, I won't change my mind.
records.finalText: In any case, I won't change my mind.
records.rationale: Repeats the established refusal-to-change-one's-mind proposition, changing only the person and discourse marker.

records.originalText: At any rate, I will do my best.
records.finalText: At any rate, I will do my best.
records.rationale: At any rate and do my best form a complete personal commitment naturally.

records.originalText: Anyhow, I'm relieved the test is over.
records.finalText: Anyhow, I'm relieved the test is over.
records.rationale: Relieved the test is over gives an explicit reason for the speaker's current feeling.

records.originalText: Anyway, I'm glad you were able to broach this difficult subject.
records.finalText: Anyway, I'm glad you were able to broach this difficult subject.
records.rationale: Broach this difficult subject is a natural advanced collocation in a complete gratitude statement.

records.originalText: Tom liked his job very much.
records.finalText: Tom liked his job very much.
records.rationale: Liked his job very much is a complete and natural specific past attitude.

records.originalText: It was such a fine day that we decided to have a picnic.
records.finalText: It was such a fine day that we decided to have a picnic.
records.rationale: Such a fine day that naturally links weather and a particular picnic decision.

records.originalText: Being very tired, I went to bed early.
records.finalText: Being very tired, I went to bed early.
records.rationale: The participial reason clause shares its subject correctly with the main early-bedtime clause.

records.originalText: There wasn't anything like enough light to read by.
records.finalText: There wasn't anything like enough light to read by.
records.rationale: Not anything like enough is a valid emphatic quantity expression with a clear reading purpose.

records.originalText: Though it was very late, he went on working.
records.finalText: Though it was very late, he went on working.
records.rationale: Though it was late and went on working express a coherent time concession.

records.originalText: It was such a hot night that I could not sleep till midnight.
records.finalText: It was such a hot night that I could not sleep till midnight.
records.rationale: Such a hot night that links a specific temperature experience and delayed sleep.

records.originalText: You're not fit to be seen.
records.finalText: You're not fit to be seen.
records.rationale: The harsh appearance judgment lacks a concrete setting and offers little suitable independent learning value.

records.originalText: Much to my surprise, the door opened noiselessly.
records.finalText: Much to my surprise, the door opened noiselessly.
records.rationale: Much to my surprise and noiselessly form a natural report of an unexpected door opening.

records.originalText: It was very cold, and what was worse, it began to rain.
records.finalText: It was very cold, and what was worse, it began to rain.
records.rationale: Pragmatic repeat of the published worsening-weather-then-rain account; cold replaces dark in the same rhetorical scenario.

records.originalText: It's so cold that the river has frozen over.
records.finalText: It's so cold that the river has frozen over.
records.rationale: So cold that expresses a situated causal observation and frozen over is idiomatic.

records.originalText: I was having a very good time, when the sad news came.
records.finalText: I was having a very good time when the sad news came.
records.rationale: Remove the unnecessary comma before the interrupting when clause; retain the ongoing enjoyment and arrival of sad news.

records.originalText: A very handsome prince met an exceptionally beautiful princess.
records.finalText: A very handsome prince met an exceptionally beautiful princess.
records.rationale: The prince and princess meeting is a coherent fictional-style past event with degree modification.

records.originalText: The Doppler effect is also observed with light and with radiant energy in general.
records.finalText: The Doppler effect is also observed with light and with radiant energy in general.
records.rationale: The technical Doppler assertion includes also and in general without its scientific context or verification.

records.originalText: Whichever you choose, you will be satisfied.
records.finalText: Whichever you choose, you will be satisfied.
records.rationale: Whichever you choose leaves both the options and satisfaction domain absent.

records.originalText: Please tell me which to take.
records.finalText: Please tell me which to take.
records.rationale: Which to take lacks an item set, route or medicine context needed to interpret the request safely and independently.

records.originalText: Which way should I go?
records.finalText: Which way should I go?
records.rationale: The short wayfinding question is a natural complete request for direction.

records.originalText: I could not decide which way to choose.
records.finalText: I could not decide which way to choose.
records.rationale: Could not decide which way to choose is grammatical deliberation about a route.

records.originalText: Which highway leads to the football stadium?
records.finalText: Which highway leads to the football stadium?
records.rationale: The highway question supplies a concrete destination and a natural leads-to collocation.

records.originalText: You had better ask him which way to take.
records.finalText: You had better ask him which way to take.
records.rationale: Had better ask him plus an embedded which-way clause gives a complete recommendation.

records.originalText: Which way is the nearest?
records.finalText: Which way is the nearest?
records.rationale: Nearest requires a destination or reference point, neither of which is supplied.

records.originalText: Which prince is the legitimate heir to the throne?
records.finalText: Which prince is the legitimate heir to the throne?
records.rationale: Legitimate heir to the throne is a natural noun phrase in an open question rather than an asserted dynastic fact.

records.originalText: Which team is likely to win?
records.finalText: Which team is likely to win?
records.rationale: Likely to win is a natural prediction question about a contextually bounded team competition.

records.originalText: Take the one you like best, whichever it is.
records.finalText: Take the one you like best, whichever it is.
records.rationale: The one and whichever it is leave the entire choice set unspecified.

records.originalText: I asked the teacher which was the better.
records.finalText: I asked the teacher which was the better.
records.rationale: Which was the better lacks the compared objects and depends on missing classroom context.

records.originalText: If anything, my father seems happier than before.
records.finalText: If anything, my father seems happier than before.
records.rationale: If anything naturally qualifies a comparison of a specific father's happiness with an earlier state.

records.originalText: One way is not better than the other.
records.finalText: One way is not better than the other.
records.rationale: One way and the other provide no actual alternatives, leaving a context-only comparison.

records.originalText: Words failed me at the last minute.
records.finalText: Words failed me at the last minute.
records.rationale: Words failed me is an idiomatic inability-to-speak account with a time anchor.

records.originalText: The Dodgers were annihilated by the Giants.
records.finalText: The Dodgers were annihilated by the Giants.
records.rationale: Annihilated is a recognized sports metaphor and both named teams identify the defeat as sporting language.

records.originalText: No matter where you may travel, be sure to phone me once a week.
records.finalText: No matter where you may travel, be sure to phone me once a week.
records.rationale: No matter where you may travel introduces a coherent concessive weekly-contact request.

records.originalText: There are isolated rain showers.
records.finalText: There are isolated rain showers.
records.rationale: Isolated rain showers is natural forecast vocabulary; this is a bounded weather utterance rather than enduring data.

records.originalText: By the way, are you free this afternoon?
records.finalText: By the way, are you free this afternoon?
records.rationale: The afternoon availability question is complete and by the way functions naturally as a topic marker.

records.originalText: By the way, where are you from?
records.finalText: By the way, where are you from?
records.rationale: The origin question is ordinary conversational English; by the way adds a natural introductory marker.

records.originalText: By the way, do you have any spare batteries?
records.finalText: By the way, do you have any spare batteries?
records.rationale: Spare batteries is a concrete noun phrase in a complete possession question.

records.originalText: By the way, how many of you are keeping a diary?
records.finalText: By the way, how many of you are keeping a diary?
records.rationale: Keeping a diary is a natural activity phrase and the question asks a specific group's current participation.

records.originalText: By the way, what is the matter with him?
records.finalText: By the way, what is the matter with him?
records.rationale: What is the matter with him is a conventional question about a person's difficulty, without diagnosis.

records.originalText: By the way, what is your address?
records.finalText: By the way, what is your address?
records.rationale: The address question is grammatical ordinary direct speech without any actual personal information.

records.originalText: By the way, what happened to the money I lent you?
records.finalText: By the way, what happened to the money I lent you?
records.rationale: The relative clause identifies a particular loan in a complete enquiry about the money.

records.originalText: By the way, how many kids are going?
records.finalText: By the way, how many kids are going?
records.rationale: How many kids are going is a complete participation question despite the destination being conversationally implicit.

records.originalText: By the way, what time will you go there?
records.finalText: By the way, what time will you go there?
records.rationale: There leaves the journey destination absent; the topic marker adds no independent context.

records.originalText: By the way, did you have any spare time to go sightseeing while you were there?
records.finalText: By the way, did you have any spare time to go sightseeing while you were there?
records.rationale: The leisure-time and sightseeing enquiry is grammatical, though the travel location remains conversationally implicit.

records.originalText: By the way, what do you do?
records.finalText: By the way, what do you do?
records.rationale: What do you do is a conventional occupation enquiry within natural direct speech.

records.originalText: As it is, I can do nothing.
records.finalText: As it is, I can do nothing.
records.rationale: As it is relies on an unstated situation, making the inability claim too context-poor.

records.originalText: Wherever he may go, he is sure to make friends.
records.finalText: Wherever he may go, he is sure to make friends.
records.rationale: Wherever he may go introduces a complete personal prediction about making friends.

records.originalText: Wherever you may go, you'll be welcomed.
records.finalText: Wherever you may go, you'll be welcomed.
records.rationale: The free-choice place clause and future passive form a coherent hospitable promise.

records.originalText: Even if you go away, I'll still passionately love you.
records.finalText: Even if you go away, I'll still passionately love you.
records.rationale: Even if expresses a coherent hypothetical separation and a specific continuing affection.

records.originalText: Where can I obtain a map of Europe?
records.finalText: Where can I obtain a map of Europe?
records.rationale: Obtain a map of Europe is a natural travel-related acquisition question.

records.originalText: It matters little where he is from.
records.finalText: It matters little where he is from.
records.rationale: It matters little plus an embedded where clause expresses a clear personal-origin evaluation.

records.originalText: Where can we exchange yen into dollars?
records.finalText: Where can we exchange yen into dollars?
records.rationale: After correcting the currency preposition, this repeats the published enquiry about exchanging yen for dollars here.

records.originalText: We haven't decided where to take a rest.
records.finalText: We haven't decided where to take a rest.
records.rationale: The present-perfect negative correctly expresses an undecided resting location.

records.originalText: Not knowing where to get off the bus, I asked the driver.
records.finalText: Not knowing where to get off the bus, I asked the driver.
records.rationale: The participial reason clause and driver enquiry share the same subject and a concrete bus context.

records.originalText: Where can dollars be exchanged for pounds?
records.finalText: Where can dollars be exchanged for pounds?
records.rationale: Repeats 38149's currency-exchange-location question with different currencies and passive voice.

records.originalText: Where did you procure the information?
records.finalText: Where did you procure the information?
records.rationale: Procure is formal but appropriate in a grammatical information-source question.

records.originalText: Before we go anywhere, we should exchange some money.
records.finalText: Before we go anywhere, we should exchange some money.
records.rationale: The before clause and should recommendation are a coherent travel-preparation utterance, without financial forecasting.

records.originalText: Something must be wrong with the machinery.
records.finalText: Something must be wrong with the machinery.
records.rationale: Must be expresses an epistemic deduction about specified machinery rather than a factual technical diagnosis.

records.originalText: Where can I get hold of a good tax lawyer?
records.finalText: Where can I get hold of a good tax lawyer?
records.rationale: Get hold of naturally asks where to locate a professional; no legal advice or endorsement is supplied.

records.originalText: Do you hear from your son from time to time?
records.finalText: Do you hear from your son from time to time?
records.rationale: Hear from and from time to time form a natural enquiry about intermittent family contact.

records.originalText: Every now and then, I play tennis for recreation.
records.finalText: Every now and then, I play tennis for recreation.
records.rationale: Every now and then naturally expresses frequency in a personal recreational habit.

records.originalText: Now and then, we go to London on business.
records.finalText: Now and then, we go to London on business.
records.rationale: Now and then marks an intermittent named-destination business trip, distinct from the tennis habit.

records.originalText: Give me five tokens, please.
records.finalText: Give me five tokens, please.
records.rationale: The polite five-token request is grammatical and gives a definite object and quantity.

records.originalText: What do you make of it?
records.finalText: What do you make of it?
records.rationale: Make of it lacks the object to interpret and depends entirely on prior discourse.

records.originalText: A fierce dog attacked the girl.
records.finalText: A fierce dog attacked the girl.
records.rationale: The specific dog-attack report is grammatical and non-graphic, with no harmful instruction.

records.originalText: There's no way I can make it up to you.
records.finalText: There's no way I can make it up to you.
records.rationale: Make it up to you is a conventional expression of inability to compensate a particular listener.

records.originalText: Now, what do you think?
records.finalText: Now, what do you think?
records.rationale: Now what do you think is a pure discourse prompt without a proposition to assess.

records.originalText: To all appearances, they are a happy couple.
records.finalText: To all appearances, they are a happy couple.
records.rationale: To all appearances explicitly frames the happy-couple description as an impression.

records.originalText: He seems to have been ill for a long time.
records.finalText: He seems to have been ill for a long time.
records.rationale: Seems to have been uses a correct perfect infinitive to express uncertainty about a personal condition.

records.originalText: How can you break the news to her?
records.finalText: How can you break the news to her?
records.rationale: Break the news is a natural idiomatic question about delivering information to a specific person.

records.originalText: How can we kill time?
records.finalText: How can we kill time?
records.rationale: Kill time is a conventional harmless idiom within a complete leisure-planning question.

records.originalText: How did you find my house?
records.finalText: How did you find my house?
records.rationale: The house-finding question is natural direct speech and identifies the destination clearly.

records.originalText: How can you justify your rude behavior?
records.finalText: How can you justify your rude behavior?
records.rationale: Justify your rude behavior is a natural evaluative question about a listener's specific conduct.

records.originalText: How did you obtain this painting?
records.finalText: How did you obtain this painting?
records.rationale: The painting-acquisition question supplies a concrete object and correct past interrogative syntax.

records.originalText: How can I meet this quota?
records.finalText: How can I meet this quota?
records.rationale: Meet this quota is a natural work-related collocation in a complete question.

records.originalText: I'm afraid I caught a cold.
records.finalText: I'm afraid I caught a cold.
records.rationale: Repeats the published personal cold report; I am afraid adds only a hedge.

records.originalText: It seems that there is something wrong with the telephone.
records.finalText: It seems that there is something wrong with the telephone.
records.rationale: It seems that correctly frames a tentative telephone malfunction assessment.

records.originalText: I get the feeling you still have an axe to grind. If you've got something to say come on out and say it.
records.finalText: I get the feeling you still have an axe to grind. If you've got something to say, come on out and say it.
records.rationale: Insert the comma after the introductory conditional clause; retain both the grievance idiom and invitation to speak.

records.originalText: I'm afraid it will rain.
records.finalText: I'm afraid it will rain.
records.rationale: Repeats the published uncertain rain forecast; I am afraid adds only a subjective hedge.

records.originalText: We gained access to the house through the window.
records.finalText: We gained access to the house through the window.
records.rationale: Gained access through the window is a coherent past account; no unauthorized motive or method is instructed.

records.originalText: At last, she hit on a good idea.
records.finalText: At last, she hit on a good idea.
records.rationale: The good-idea discovery repeats the published good-idea-crossed-my-mind proposition with person and idiom changes.

records.originalText: He was put to death finally.
records.finalText: He was put to death finally.
records.rationale: The unexplained execution statement is unsuitable as an unframed general learner typing example.

records.originalText: Eventually the salesman persuaded me to buy the expensive machine.
records.finalText: Eventually the salesman persuaded me to buy the expensive machine.
records.rationale: Persuaded me to buy correctly takes an object and infinitive in a complete purchasing account.

records.originalText: In the end, because of the disease, he became unable to walk and had to use a motorized wheelchair to get around.
records.finalText: In the end, because of the disease, he became unable to walk and had to use a motorized wheelchair to get around.
records.rationale: The mobility account concerns one person's illness, with coherent past causality and neutral wheelchair wording.

records.originalText: Sing the song once more, please.
records.finalText: Sing the song once more, please.
records.rationale: Once more naturally modifies a complete polite request to repeat a song.

records.originalText: Please go on with your dinner.
records.finalText: Please go on with your dinner.
records.rationale: Go on with your dinner is a valid request to continue the meal.

records.originalText: Please bring your plan up at the meeting.
records.finalText: Please bring your plan up at the meeting.
records.rationale: Bring your plan up is a naturally separated phrasal verb with an explicit meeting context.

records.originalText: Please give your mother my best regards.
records.finalText: Please give your mother my best regards.
records.rationale: Repeats the existing published give-my-regards message request, changing only the recipient to the listener's mother.

records.originalText: Pass me the butter, will you please?
records.finalText: Pass me the butter, will you please?
records.rationale: Pragmatic repeat of the published pass-me-the-jam request; changing the table condiment adds little content.

records.originalText: Please see that the job is finished.
records.finalText: Please see that the job is finished.
records.rationale: See that plus a passive clause is a conventional instruction to ensure task completion.

records.originalText: I am at a loss what to do.
records.finalText: I am at a loss what to do.
records.rationale: Repeats the published at-a-loss-what-to-say uncertainty expression with a less specific action complement.

records.originalText: Not knowing what to do, I asked the teacher for advice.
records.finalText: Not knowing what to do, I asked the teacher for advice.
records.rationale: The participial reason clause shares the main subject and teacher-advice supplies a complete response.

records.originalText: I can't start up my computer. What am I supposed to do?
records.finalText: I can't start up my computer. What am I supposed to do?
records.rationale: Start up my computer and the follow-up action question form a coherent troubleshooting utterance.

records.originalText: Not knowing what to do, I asked him for help.
records.finalText: Not knowing what to do, I asked him for help.
records.rationale: Repeats 38607's not-knowing-what-to-do request for assistance with a less specific helper.

records.originalText: How come she hung up on you?
records.finalText: How come she hung up on you?
records.rationale: How come correctly uses statement order and hung up on specifies the telephone action.

records.originalText: How did she get mixed up with such unpleasant people?
records.finalText: How did she get mixed up with such unpleasant people?
records.rationale: Get mixed up with is a natural idiom for becoming involved with particular people.

records.originalText: Will you tell me why you like her?
records.finalText: Will you tell me why you like her?
records.rationale: The indirect why clause has correct statement order inside a polite request.

records.originalText: Why is he looking at me as though he knows me?
records.finalText: Why is he looking at me as though he knows me?
records.rationale: As though he knows me grammatically frames a perceived recognition rather than asserting it.

records.originalText: I wonder what has made him change his mind.
records.finalText: I wonder what has made him change his mind.
records.rationale: The embedded what clause naturally identifies uncertainty about a person's changed decision.

records.originalText: What made him so angry then, I wonder?
records.finalText: What made him so angry then, I wonder?
records.rationale: The past causative anger question and parenthetical I wonder form natural speech.

records.originalText: How did they come by all that wealth?
records.finalText: How did they come by all that wealth?
records.rationale: Come by all that wealth is idiomatic acquisition language within an open question.

records.originalText: And why do you think that is?
records.finalText: And why do you think that is?
records.rationale: And and that both depend on a missing preceding explanation or proposition.

records.originalText: Why has Japan let pollution get so bad?
records.finalText: Why has Japan let pollution get so bad?
records.rationale: The country-wide pollution question presupposes an unspecified historical deterioration and cause.

records.originalText: Why has the birthrate declined so sharply?
records.finalText: Why has the birthrate declined so sharply?
records.rationale: The birthrate question presupposes a steep decline without any population or time frame.

records.originalText: What makes you think that I'm against that?
records.finalText: What makes you think that I'm against that?
records.rationale: Both occurrences of that lack referents, leaving the opposition question without independent content.

records.originalText: Why don't you ever say it?
records.finalText: Why don't you ever say it?
records.rationale: Say it has no message referent and the habitual reproach depends on prior dialogue.

records.originalText: I can't understand how your father managed to see through that man.
records.finalText: I can't understand how your father managed to see through that man.
records.rationale: See through that man is an established idiom; the nested clauses remain grammatical and coherent.

records.originalText: Why did you part with your house?
records.finalText: Why did you part with your house?
records.rationale: Part with your house is idiomatic disposal language in a concrete past question.

records.originalText: Not knowing what to do, I asked for help.
records.finalText: Not knowing what to do, I asked for help.
records.rationale: Repeats 38607's uncertainty-followed-by-help request while omitting the helper.

records.originalText: I can't for the life of me remember her phone number.
records.finalText: I can't for the life of me remember her phone number.
records.rationale: For the life of me is a conventional idiomatic emphasis on failing to recall a phone number.

records.originalText: I couldn't bring myself to tell her the truth.
records.finalText: I couldn't bring myself to tell her the truth.
records.rationale: Could not bring myself to plus infinitive naturally expresses reluctance to tell the truth.

records.originalText: For some reason or other I cannot bring myself to work.
records.finalText: For some reason or other I cannot bring myself to work.
records.rationale: For some reason or other and bring myself to work form a coherent report of unexplained reluctance.

records.originalText: I'm just a creature of habit, I guess.
records.finalText: I'm just a creature of habit, I guess.
records.rationale: Creature of habit is an idiomatic self-description, appropriately hedged by I guess.

records.originalText: For the life of me, I couldn't remember his name.
records.finalText: For the life of me, I couldn't remember his name.
records.rationale: Repeats 38706's for-the-life-of-me failure of recall with only the remembered item changed.

records.originalText: I cannot for the life of me remember where it was.
records.finalText: I cannot for the life of me remember where it was.
records.rationale: Another for-the-life-of-me memory failure repeats 38706 while leaving the location referent vague.

records.originalText: I simply cannot get rid of this bad cold of mine.
records.finalText: I simply cannot get rid of this bad cold of mine.
records.rationale: Same unresolved-cold complaint as the published I-have-not-got-rid-of-my-bad-cold-yet example.

records.originalText: Why do they call New York the Big Apple?
records.finalText: Why do they call New York the Big Apple?
records.rationale: The question about a city's nickname is complete and makes no origin assertion.

records.originalText: What makes you think that way?
records.finalText: What makes you think that way?
records.rationale: Pragmatic repeat of the already-published what-is-it-that-makes-you-think-that-way question.

records.originalText: How did you arrive at such a conclusion?
records.finalText: How did you arrive at such a conclusion?
records.rationale: Arrive at such a conclusion is a natural reasoning collocation in a complete question.

records.originalText: How can you bear such a humiliation?
records.finalText: How can you bear such a humiliation?
records.rationale: Bear such a humiliation is a grammatical question about tolerating a particular experience.

records.originalText: How can you be so passive? Why don't you retaliate?
records.finalText: How can you be so passive? Why don't you retaliate?
records.rationale: The unframed demand to retaliate is unsuitable as general learner advice and supplies no conflict context.

records.originalText: What do you want such an old car for?
records.finalText: What do you want such an old car for?
records.rationale: What do you want an old car for is natural colloquial questioning with a clear object.

records.originalText: Why does that require an apology?
records.finalText: Why does that require an apology?
records.rationale: Require an apology is a natural complete question about whether an act warrants one.

records.originalText: How did such a thing come about?
records.finalText: How did such a thing come about?
records.rationale: Repeats the how-did-a-strange-thing-come-about question accepted in 36684.

records.originalText: How did you come to hear of it?
records.finalText: How did you come to hear of it?
records.rationale: Come to hear of is a natural discovery expression in a grammatically complete question.

records.originalText: What put such an idea into your head?
records.finalText: What put such an idea into your head?
records.rationale: Put an idea into your head is an established figurative expression in a coherent question.

records.originalText: How did this misunderstanding ever arise?
records.finalText: How did this misunderstanding ever arise?
records.rationale: Arise is correctly intransitive and this misunderstanding supplies an explicit event anchor.

records.originalText: Why did you call me at this unearthly hour?
records.finalText: Why did you call me at this unearthly hour?
records.rationale: Unearthly hour is an idiomatic complaint anchored by a specific telephone call.

records.originalText: How is it that you can speak this language?
records.finalText: How is it that you can speak this language?
records.rationale: How is it that correctly introduces a complete question about a listener's language ability.

records.originalText: Not knowing what to do, he asked me for help.
records.finalText: Not knowing what to do, he asked me for help.
records.rationale: Repeats 38607's uncertainty-leading-to-a-help-request scenario with pronoun substitutions.

records.originalText: Not knowing what to do, we telephoned the police.
records.finalText: Not knowing what to do, we telephoned the police.
records.rationale: Calling the police is a distinct concrete response to uncertainty; the participial subject correctly matches we.

records.originalText: What made you do a silly thing like that?
records.finalText: What made you do a silly thing like that?
records.rationale: Make you do uses a correct bare infinitive in a natural question about a listener's action.

records.originalText: How come you didn't come to the party?
records.finalText: How come you didn't come to the party?
records.rationale: How come with didn't uses natural colloquial statement order in a party-absence enquiry.

records.originalText: What happened? The car's slowing down.
records.finalText: What happened? The car's slowing down.
records.rationale: The event question and car-slowing observation form a complete coherent utterance.

records.originalText: I don't know how to satisfy his need for constant attention.
records.finalText: I don't know how to satisfy his need for constant attention.
records.rationale: Satisfy his need for constant attention is a natural complement inside a correct embedded how clause.

records.originalText: Not knowing what to do, she remained silent.
records.finalText: Not knowing what to do, she remained silent.
records.rationale: Repeats the not-knowing-and-remaining-silent scenario accepted in 36008 with only the person varied.

records.originalText: Please let me make it up to you.
records.finalText: Please let me make it up to you.
records.rationale: Repeats 38304's listener-compensation idiom as a request rather than an inability statement.

records.originalText: Please turn the television on.
records.finalText: Please turn the television on.
records.rationale: Turn the television on is natural separable phrasal-verb use in a clear request.

records.originalText: Please keep me informed of what is happening there.
records.finalText: Please keep me informed of what is happening there.
records.rationale: Keep me informed plus an embedded event clause forms a complete communication request.

records.originalText: Please write about your real experience.
records.finalText: Please write about your real experience.
records.rationale: Real experience is a grammatical noun phrase asking for a personally experienced account.

records.originalText: The toilet was outside, in the yard.
records.finalText: The toilet was outside, in the yard.
records.rationale: The past toilet-location statement has a clear outdoor location and is independently understandable.

records.originalText: The argument presented in Doyle's study was first published as a white paper on drug-related crimes.
records.finalText: The argument presented in Doyle's study was first published as a white paper on drug-related crimes.
records.rationale: Doyle's study and the publication sequence are specific bibliographic claims without enough identifying source evidence.

records.originalText: Germany was allied with Italy in World War II.
records.finalText: Germany was allied with Italy in World War II.
records.rationale: The named countries and World War II form a stable, conventional historical alliance statement.

records.originalText: As we thought, she had gone abroad.
records.finalText: As we thought, she had gone abroad.
records.rationale: The past-perfect travel event naturally precedes the retrospective as-we-thought evaluation.

records.originalText: Shall I close the door?
records.finalText: Shall I close the door?
records.rationale: Shall I close the door is a natural complete offer to perform a household action.

records.originalText: It is very careless of you to leave the door open.
records.finalText: It is very careless of you to leave the door open.
records.rationale: Careless of you to leave correctly uses the adjective-person-infinitive evaluative construction.

records.originalText: Whoever is at the door, please ask him to wait.
records.finalText: Whoever is at the door, please ask him to wait.
records.rationale: Whoever is at the door supplies an indefinite person and the polite waiting request follows coherently.

records.originalText: There was a big gold star on the door.
records.finalText: There was a big gold star on the door.
records.rationale: The existential past description specifies a visible door decoration naturally.

records.originalText: How careless he was to pinch his fingers in the door!
records.finalText: How careless he was to pinch his fingers in the door!
records.rationale: The past exclamation about fingers caught in a door is grammatical and a non-graphic household mishap.

records.originalText: If a door doesn't fit the casing, we must plane it carefully until it does.
records.finalText: If a door doesn't fit the casing, we must plane it carefully until it does.
records.rationale: The conditional describes fitting a wooden door and plane is a valid verb; it makes no unverified technical guarantee.

records.originalText: When the door slammed unexpectedly, it startled me.
records.finalText: When the door slammed unexpectedly, it startled me.
records.rationale: The unexpected door slam and startle result form a coherent specific past event.

records.originalText: As soon as the door opened, they ran away.
records.finalText: As soon as the door opened, they ran away.
records.rationale: As soon as correctly links the door opening and immediate departure.

records.originalText: Some TV programs are interesting, and others are not.
records.finalText: Some TV programs are interesting, and others are not.
records.rationale: Some and others form a balanced subjective comparison of television programs.

records.originalText: TV programs have a bad influence on children.
records.finalText: TV programs have a bad influence on children.
records.rationale: The blanket claim that TV programs harm children lacks qualification or evidence.

records.originalText: It cost me ten thousand yen to have my television set repaired.
records.finalText: It cost me ten thousand yen to have my television set repaired.
records.rationale: The cost-me and have-something-repaired constructions describe a specific past bill rather than a current market price.

records.originalText: Play outside instead of watching TV.
records.finalText: Play outside instead of watching TV.
records.rationale: The everyday invitation to play outside uses instead of plus a gerund correctly.

records.originalText: When you watch television or listen to the radio, the music which you hear is often African in origin.
records.finalText: When you watch television or listen to the radio, the music which you hear is often African in origin.
records.rationale: The frequency and origin claim about broadcast music is broad, time-dependent and unsupported by sentence provenance.

records.originalText: Television enlightens the viewers as well as entertains them.
records.finalText: Television enlightens the viewers as well as entertains them.
records.rationale: The blanket claim that television enlightens and entertains viewers lacks program or audience scope.

records.originalText: The invention of TV caused a drastic change in our daily life.
records.finalText: The invention of TV caused a drastic change in our daily life.
records.rationale: The sweeping invention-caused-life-change statement needs historical framing and a defined population.

records.originalText: Television enables us to learn about foreign manners and customs.
records.finalText: Television enables us to learn about foreign manners and customs.
records.rationale: Enables us to learn expresses a reasonable media capability rather than a universal outcome for all viewing.

records.originalText: What is shown on television is, as it were, a reflection of what society is like.
records.finalText: What is shown on television is, as it were, a reflection of what society is like.
records.rationale: The sociological generalization about television reflecting society lacks a stated viewpoint or bounded context.
